tweet_summary: Posts a dramatic video captioned 'Did you see where she landed 😯 that was close' showing a person seemingly flung off a cliffside platform toward a suspended target far below, presented as a real near-miss stunt.
why_note_decision: The clip is presented as a real, jaw-dropping near-death moment but is not an authentic uncontrolled event. The strongest evidence (AI media description of physically implausible cantilevered-platform geometry; near-unanimous replies calling it AI/'AI slop' and noting it 'defies physics - she bounces higher than she fell') points to AI-generated or fabricated content, not a genuine accident. A note is warranted so viewers don't treat synthetic/fabricated footage as a real event. However, the verdict hinges on media that an AI description can misread and that I cannot independently source, so confidence is limited.
judge_guidance: A correct note must establish that the video is NOT an authentic, real-world uncontrolled fall/near-miss - it is fabricated or AI-generated content (the physics are impossible and the clip shows hallmarks of AI generation). PASS only if the note clearly tells viewers the footage is not a real accident/genuine event and is staged or AI-generated. CRITICALLY, the note must AVOID the original's specific failure: do NOT assert a confident, fabricated physical mechanism ('a man jumps on an inflatable mat to launch the woman into a safety net') sourced to unrelated Instagram reels that don't depict this clip - that invented explanation is why the original was tagged IrrelevantSources/Incorrect. A correct note may say the precise method is unclear but the clip is not real; FAIL if it confidently invents the staging mechanics or cites sources that don't actually show or substantiate this specific video.
reference_note: This is not real footage of an accident. The clip is fabricated/AI-generated: the depicted fall is physically impossible (the figure rebounds higher than it dropped) and the imagery shows hallmarks of AI-generated video. It is not a genuine stunt or near-miss.

Raters tagged IrrelevantSources (5) and Incorrect (5).

fact_check.claim_verdict: not a real event; fabricated / likely AI-generated
fact_check.notes: Could not source the exact clip, but the media description (impossible cantilevered geometry, figure plummeting toward a suspended target) and near-unanimous replies ('AI', 'AI slop', 'defies physics') indicate fabricated/AI content. The original note's specific 'mat-and-net' mechanism is unsupported.

importance.lens_rationale: Low-stakes viral entertainment 'slop'; minor value in teaching audiences to recognize AI-generated footage, but no real-world harm beyond credulity.
